$comment: Reviewed, time-boxed exceptions for `npm run audit:ci`.
Every entry needs a reason, the mitigation that makes it acceptable, and a reviewBy date.
The gate fails when an entry expires, when an allowlisted advisory stops appearing
(the exception is stale and must be deleted), or when its severity changes.
See the 'Dependency audit state' section of README.md for the full analysis.

advisories.title: image-size: ICNS parser allows denial of service through an infinite loop
advisories.reason: Reached only via metro (the bundler) at build time; not present in the shipped app binary. Every published image-size version (<=2.0.2) is affected, so there is no version to upgrade to, and no API-compatible replacement package exists.
advisories.mitigation: metro.config.js calls image-size's disableTypes() on Metro's own instance to switch off the icns parser. Metro never requests dimensions for ICNS assets, so this costs nothing and the payload is rejected instantly instead of looping.

advisories.title: image-size: JXL and HEIF parsers allow denial of service through infinite loops
advisories.reason: Same root cause, package and reachability as GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr.
advisories.mitigation: metro.config.js disables the jxl, jxl-stream and heif parsers alongside icns.

advisories.title: decode-uri-component: Denial of service via exponential decoding of malformed percent-encoded input
advisories.reason: Transitive via @react-navigation/native -> @react-navigation/core -> query-string@7.1.3, which pins decode-uri-component ^0.2.2. Note this is a separate advisory from the 2022 one (<0.2.1) that 0.2.2 was published to fix; this one's range is <=0.4.2. Neither available route out is safe: the patched 0.5.0 is ESM-only (type: module, exports with no CommonJS entry) while query-string@7.1.3 is CommonJS calling require('decode-uri-component'), so an overrides pin passes CI and then throws ERR_REQUIRE_ESM at runtime; and npm's own fixAvailable is a major downgrade of @react-navigation/native to 3.8.4, which would remove the v7 API the app is built on. React Navigation v6 depends on the same query-string range, so downgrading the navigation stack does not avoid it either. No safe upgrade exists until React Navigation ships a core using a fixed query-string.
advisories.mitigation: The vulnerable parser is unreachable in this app. React Navigation only calls query-string from its deep-link handling, and deep linking is not configured: RootNavigator renders NavigationContainer with no linking prop, and nothing in src/ sets link prefixes or calls getInitialURL. No user-, network- or OS-supplied URL reaches decode-uri-component, so there is no input to make malformed.
